note:
R91 - gen7 `.ast` stream-file block payload framing (Q-R89-1), measured from the bank tree's stream offsets (R89) on the loose
X360 NHL 10-Legacy and PS3 NHL 11 / 14 / 15 / Legacy trees. Read-only; every access bounds-checked; unknown variants are classified,
never forced through a familiar layout.

Grammar under test (derived on PS3 / X360 NHL 15 `playercalls` + `crowds`, then tested on every stream of every tree):
  .ast   'S10S' | u32 id (== bank header 0x2c) | zeros to 0x40 | streams
  stream  blocks { u8 flags (0x00 continue, 0x80 terminal) | u24 size (counts the 8 header bytes) | u32 samples | payload }
          starts 0x40-aligned; PS3: streams tile contiguously (the terminal block's payload ends in zero padding up to the next 0x40
          boundary); X360: the terminal block's size is a multiple of 0x40 and zero-word gaps separate streams (both measured here).
  payload by the S10A record's codec (SNR h1):
    0x05 EALayer3 v1  : a chain of EA-frames (u8 pcm_flag 0x00 / 0xEE | u8 common (version 2 / 3, sr index, mode, ext) | side info
                        | byte-aligned main data [| PCM block fields + PCM]) exactly as R77 read the ram segments; N interleaved
                        streams for channel_config 3 (2) / 5 (3); zero padding allowed ONLY as the trailing bytes of the terminal
                        block (a frame cannot start with common byte 0: MPEG version 0 is reserved) - a zero run elsewhere is refused;
    0x03 EA-XMA       : { u32 w0 (w0 >> 2 = sub-block length incl. w0; low 2 bits recorded) | one XMA2 packet } x sub-blocks, then zero
                        padding (terminal block only, measured) - packet headers read (frame count, first-frame offset, metadata, skip);
    other codecs      : classified `unsupported-codec`, header walk only.
  sample words: middle blocks == granules / nstreams x 576 (EAL3) - measured; first block: decoded - declared = 1152 x 1 (+ PCM) per
  stream (EAL3) / 384 (XMA, R84) - measured as a distribution, not assumed; terminal block: declared <= decodable (tail trim recorded).
  loop records (16-byte S10A stub, words a / b): the stream at O is a one-block stub with (samples, size) == (a, b); the body is the
  next stream (PS3: at the stub's end; X360: at the next 0x40 boundary), referenced by no list entry, with its own warm-up signature
  (block-0 delta equal to the class's non-loop first-block delta) - verified per record; stub + body samples == num_samples.
Tests per stream: S1 O 0x40-aligned and inside the file; S2 the walk from O reaches a 0x80 block with every block header inside the
  file and size >= 8; S3 flags in {0x00, 0x80}; S4 Σ block samples == num_samples (non-loop) / stub + body (loop); S5 every payload
  classified by codec: EAL3 frames tile every block (zero padding only in the terminal block), XMA sub-blocks tile every block;
  S6 per-block sample rule (middle blocks exact; first-block delta; terminal trim recorded); S7 stream end vs next start (gap bytes,
  all-zero); S8 loop stub / body relations. Consumed bytes accounted: headers, payload frames / packets, terminal zero padding,
  inter-stream gaps, file tail, unexplained (nonzero) tails.
Controls (in memory, per platform, original file hash re-checked afterwards): truncated block header, truncated payload, size 0 / size 4 /
  size 0xFFFFFF, O beyond file / O + 1 / O + 8 (mid-block), 0x80 flag cleared on the terminal block, 0x80 set on a middle block, samples
  word + 1, loop word a + 1, one byte flipped in a middle frame's common byte, one byte flipped in a frame's side info, one byte flipped
  deep in main data (expected NOT structurally detectable - reported as such), X360: w0 + 4, packet frame count 0.
Usage: python r91_ast_framing.py <out.json> [--trees a,b] [--banks x,y] [--per-bank N] [--blockmaps DIR] [--summary FILE.jsonl] [--no-controls]
